raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

In Rust mode (`SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`), the PD KV bootstrap registry starts inside a scheduler, so other prefill ranks can finish loading before its listener is up. Their registration gives up after five attempts and only logs an error. That leaves the rank directory incomplete, and every PD request is unroutable while the server otherwise looks healthy.

## Modifications

- In Rust mode, prefill ranks keep retrying registration until `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT`, and fail startup at the deadline. The Python frontend keeps its five attempts.
- The Rust registry no longer counts a retried registration as a new rank, so it doesn't advertise readiness while a rank is still missing.
- Test: Rust-mode registration waits for a delayed listener and fails at the deadline.

## Tests

- `python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_register_to_bootstrap.py`: 14 passed.
- In `rust/`: `cargo test -p sglang-server` (334 passed), `cargo clippy -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are clean.
- `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`: all hooks pass.
- `test/registered/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_rust_server.py` on two A100s, run on a tree with all the related Rust-frontend PRs merged (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, nixl transfer; triton attention and pytorch sampling because of the local FlashInfer build; `test_gsm8k` skipped because it needs a dataset download): 5 passed, both with the shared API/bootstrap port and with a distinct `--disaggregation-bootstrap-port`.
- Not reproduced on GPUs: the multi-rank startup race itself, which needs a prefill server with several ranks where the registry starts late.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
